item: the scheduler's exclusive hold is counted and each claim is released by the operation that took it, so a window that ends inside a standalone restore no longer releases the restore's hold (R383, OPEN_QUEUE 2026-10-27 item 23)
summary: BEFORE: BackgroundScheduler._exclusive_hold was one boolean. A standalone restore (src/backup/volume_job.py) claims it through the bare pause_for_exclusive_operation, which exclusive_window_open() cannot see; a diagnostics bundle opened inside it claimed it again and its resume released it, so Run now and Start were accepted mid-restore, and a Start the operator pressed during the restore was taken by the bundle's resume and started the loop mid-restore. NOW: hold_exclusive adds one claim and release_exclusive takes one off (floored at zero), answering (hold_ended, start_wanted) in the same locked step, so two operations that end together never strand a deferred start; a release that is not the last queues the start of a loop its operation stopped behind the remaining holder (hand_over_start). A claim is released by the operation that took it: pause_for_exclusive_operation records it in a caller-kept list (claim=, appended inside the scheduler's lock), resume_after_exclusive_operation(claim=) releases exactly those claims, ALWAYS, also inside an open window (where any start is handed to the window, whose last exit makes it even when that window holds no claim of its own), and empties the list, so a repeated resume releases nothing. The bare pause takes its own claim also inside an open window (it stops nothing there), so a window that ends before a restore begun inside it (an export, a bundle) no longer starts collection under the restore; this reverse order was open on main too. exclusive_window keeps its windows' claims in one set released by the last window out; volume_job passes its claim. status() adds exclusive_holds. tests/test_scheduler_counted_hold.py (12 tests) drives a real BackgroundScheduler: the nested trace both ways (restore ends first, bundle ends first), a restore begun inside a window that ends first, a start handed to a window without a claim, two resumes one after the other in both orders, the release-and-deferral step, the stray release, a repeated resume. On origin/main the three trace tests fail on behaviour (the bundle's resume released the restore's hold; it started the loop mid-restore); the other new tests fail there at the claim= API, which did not exist; the two added after the security reads also fail on this PR's previous head. Test doubles of pause/resume in five test files take the new keyword. Stated limits: memstop and the data-drive move pause with no resume by design, so their claim stays for the life of the process; if memstop's shutdown request fails the process lives on with that claim, Start refused, now visible as exclusive_holds in status(). A caller that passes no claim list (none in src/ after this change) keeps the pre-R383 reading: a claim is assumed exactly when no window is open at its resume, so it still leaks its claim if it ends inside a window. A claim that is never released (an interrupt in the few unguarded steps between a pause and its resume's release) now lasts until restart, where the boolean was cleared by the next operation's release; status() shows it as exclusive_holds. Release-notes line: «A diagnostics bundle taken during a restore no longer lets collection restart in the middle of that restore.»
